guidance: A registration belongs to a particular binding, not just a model ID. A new binding may reuse the same key. Exercise a retained action across rebinding and compare its recipient with the newly installed action's.
A moved button can still have a parent. Decide whether the component still owns that button before delivering its command; attachment by itself answers a different question.
An action retained while enabled can outlive permission to perform it. Read eligibility at dispatch; restoring permission should restore ordinary operation.
Try the actual buttons independently. A passing keyboard or accessibility shortcut tells you nothing about whether the ordinary button dispatched Open, Save, Details or Play.
For a representable, distinguish make, update and dismantle. Refresh registrations on the object that owns them; tearing down an obsolete coordinator must not unplug its replacement.
A plausible action title does not establish its destination. Follow the named installed action through to its return value and recipient.
Separate asking to close from completing the transition. A refusal leaves the presentation active; an accepted but unfinished dismissal has not yet earned a restoration request.
Capture the presentation at callback installation. Reading a shared current ticket inside a late callback gives the retired presentation the replacement's authority.
Consume the outgoing presentation before the external restoration call. That call can synchronously open another presentation; cleanup afterward can erase it.
Choose the destination when restoration is due. On Mac, distinguish being visible from accepting first responder; try the eligible fallback if the original refuses.
Restore the owner's saved background configuration. Unconditionally setting a flag to false can expose content that was hidden even before the panel opened.
Compare the submitted values with the editable control at delivery. Editing through a helper that cancels the request cannot demonstrate what happens when a native field changes directly.
A superseded completion must not release the replacement's busy state. A cancellation for the still-current operation, by contrast, must leave the user able to try again.
Mark a submission consumed before calling client code. If client code immediately submits again, the old completion must leave that request intact.
Apply errors to the live field they describe. On recovery remove the obsolete message from that field while retaining unrelated errors and input.
Unregistering stops future registration deliveries, not necessarily work already queued. After restart, deliver an old notification and a new one and distinguish their effects.
Carry the producing API's coordinate system and document identity to the consuming API. Recover the actual substring; comparing two integers can agree even when they point at the wrong text.
An edit can leave a cached match in bounds but no longer matching. Resolve against the current document before moving the cursor.
Use the current target and navigation direction rather than selecting the first match on every request. Keep ordinary heading traversal usable after a reorder.
For intersecting matches, ask whether the product advances from the start or end of the last match. Both policies can be correct; a repeated-pattern input distinguishes them.
Follow the actual source of text size: a caller-supplied preview setting and the live environment are different inputs. Exercise a second size on the same view and retain its action.
Recompute a scaled font from its design size, not the previous scaled output. A round trip between two sizes exposes compounding.
Identify the interactive owner before grouping. A shelf or wrapper may organize navigation while each episode still owns its own activation.
For an AppKit row, inspect role, selection and independently usable children separately. A correctly titled row does not prove any of those three properties.
Preserve surviving selection across sibling moves by identity. Duplicate display titles distinguish identity from accidental reselection by name or position.
Resolve interior coordinates of a spanning cell as well as its origin. Treat coordinates outside the grid separately from valid covered positions.
Change only the trait bits owned by this state transition. Start with unrelated traits present and toggle both ways; replacing the entire set can pass an initially empty fixture.
Decide which audience is missing a name: sighted users, assistive clients or test automation. Inspect the displayed title if the complaint concerns what people see.
Reset decoration on reconfiguration without hiding the whole row. Begin with the decoration exposed so an omitted reset is observable.
Follow a picker write past the menu state into the selected option on the same player item. Changing an app-side ID alone can leave playback untouched.
Before offering a clear operation check whether the group permits an empty choice. A rejected clear leaves both the player and its displayed choice unchanged.
Filtering the menu can hide the currently selected option. Preserve that state distinctly from no selected option; rebuilding the menu is not a user command.
A clear callback is still a write. Retain the setter, replace the player item, then invoke it: the replacement keeps its choice while its own current setter remains usable.
Two loads can race on the very same item. Item identity filters replacement items but cannot order requests for one item; accept only the current request's result.
Separate not loaded, load failed and successfully inspected with zero options. Report the observed state rather than inventing an empty menu; allow recovery from a failed load.
If the menu promises full captions, distinguish forced-only tracks from full tracks. Filtering what is offered does not authorize changing playback's existing selection.
Identify described audio from its characteristic on the option itself. Commentary or a language match alone is not evidence of description.
Keep buffer observations and player readiness as separate facts. They may disagree; do not convert either into a guarantee that playing now will succeed.
Reduce Motion changes how an update is presented, not whether it happens. Inspect the new content and selected value as well as the motion policy.
Distinguish an immediate update from a shortened animation when the product requires no transition. If the existing effective preference already selects the right branch, preserve it.
For sRGB luminance, a midtone distinguishes linearized light from encoded channel values; black and white alone cannot detect a missing transfer step.
For translucent content, establish the actual background before calculating a rendered ratio. If the calculator accepts only opaque samples, report that boundary.
Resolve semantic colors in the requested appearance before comparing them. One light-mode pair cannot verify the dark-mode decision.
An empty help string and an absent value are not interchangeable when the configuration contract distinguishes them. Rebind the same control without help; its ordinary action must survive.
Two empty strings can agree while conveying no state. Compare visible and accessibility status against the intended meaning in each selection state.
Select an editing category only for actions that represent editing. Leave the default alone for ordinary commands and verify the declared SDK member rather than guessing its spelling.
While the command remains retained, change the editor to read-only and invoke it. Opening a menu is not the event that revokes editability.
In SwiftUI hosting AppKit, hide redundant chrome only if the native search field and its Clear path remain independently usable. Hiding the entire wrapper is not evidence that the editor survives.

A labeled native slider with a working binding is a preservation case unless the input identifies a concrete unmet requirement. The absence of a custom value modifier is not a defect or a prediction of speech.
Returning control to automatic selection can choose another track. If the request is Off, distinguish an explicitly empty selection from system choice and inspect the item's resulting option.
Repeated selection of the active speed is not a new transition. Drive the actual selection binding twice, count effects, then change speed and confirm one real update still passes through.
